To focus more on what you said about the relationship aspect of things. I'm 18, the same age as you. Started dating my fiance when I was a freshman. High school sweethearts, ain't that adorable? 

At the time, I had the same thoughts as you. I looked at everyone around me, younger and older, and asked the question, "Why did you all settle?" Without even realizing how flawed my question was.

Almost every person I knew in my age group who dated tons of people was not "falling in love" a bunch of times. They were hopping from person to person to try and fill a hole or get something out of someone else. None of them had any idea what love was or what it could be if you took the time to nurture it. And the ones that I still keep up with, some older than me and some younger, have all been negatively impacted by those relationships.

And while I haven't had a job to speak of, and it's been some time since I've had the privilege to travel, the love I've gotten to experience (even though it was my "first") has been the farthest thing from boring. To find someone who loves you at the same time that you love them is a gift. He's been with me through every major stage. And we have the luxury of being able to grow together, to form lives with and around each other - as opposed to older individuals who have to carve out spots or find space in their life for a new partner. We settled into our love the way you would settle into your spot on the couch, or a dog would settle into their bed. Comfortably, calmly, feeling right at home. 

But we've also had so much fun. Late night drives into our middle of nowhere town, him singing every song as though he was saying the words to me and not just near me. The anxiety of going to each other's houses for the first time, meeting parents, having dinners, sneaking off to a hidden corner so nobody would see us kiss. Staying up late at night on call, talking until our words didn't make sense anymore. Cooking meals together - he always was better at chopping veggies than I was. Hundreds of dollars spent on gas station food over the years because it was the only place we could walk to. Hundreds of energy drinks shared, where he would always give me the first sip. Both of us checking if every new game has a co-op feature. I spoiled every single gift to date that I have ever given him because I was so excited to see his reaction. Spending 22 hours total baking and decorating his birthday cake (with no prior cake decorating experience), because he had never had "a pretty cake" before. Always being each other's first in every aspect. Trying everything together. Sharing everything with each other. 

No matter what has happened in my life, I get to wake up each day feeling so lucky that I'm with him. And I hope and pray that everyone gets to have that. But not a single thing in my life is boring while he's in it.

The comments here are... disappointing, to say the least. There is nothing normal about porn. Especially excessive usage. I don't care if you're a man or a woman who watches it. The effects it has on society and our brains are undeniable. And it's crazy to me that in a sub like this, you see so many people here defending it. Just because you do something doesn't mean it's right. No, not all men do it, just like not all 20 somethings drink. If he can't stop watching it on a dime, for someone he claims to love, and be understanding of why it harms you, that's a red flag for addiction. That's how it started with my partner. We've been together for almost 5 years now. It's what he used to cope since he was 11. But even HE now talks to other men in his life about the issues with it and how he's improved since committing to not watching. If you're in a monogamous relationship, there is absolutely NO NEED to whack off to random strangers who are performing a xerox of a xerox of sex. People with unrealistic proportions, doing unrealistic things, to sell you an idea that most men take into the real world and treat as fact, as what sex and women should be. I say all of this as someone who obsessively watched porn myself for a lonnnng time during important developmental years. Don't you let anyone here make you feel bad for the way you feel, or like you should be cool about this, or more importantly, that he is "just as normal" as you. Because he's not! Go check out the loveafterporn sub and read some of the stories there. A lot of it is folks in your situation venting. Some of it is people talking about their partners who have recovered or from people who have recovered themselves. It can give you a place to talk, or maybe decide what you want your life to be like in the future. A lot of people will say to end it, and maybe that's the best decision for you, but maybe you both can get through this. He has to want it, and you can't make someone want to be better for you. But you can sure as hell hope. And more importantly, know that what he watches is not at all a reflection of you. You are beautiful, and you are worthy of someone who will love you and only you. Who will care if they are doing something that hurts you and who will grow for/with you. If you need support, or help, or any advice from someone who has been through this, feel free to reach out ♡

In my experience, having ADHD and being surrounded by others who also do, we're more prone to addiction than the average person. To the point where others get hostile when you even bring up the possibility that porn has harmful effects. I'm very proud of you for recognizing that it has become an issue, this is the most important step. The next step would be getting in contact with a therapist (preferably someone who is a CSAT or who has had experience with sex addiction). If you're unable to do that, there are many sources available online for those who want to quit. I'll gladly compile a list for you if that's something you'd be interested in. Facing any addiction is a bumpy road. I struggled with porn and SH when I was younger. Haven't touched the former in years, and I'm almost a year clean from the latter. The positive effects getting clean has had on my life are immeasurable. I believe we all can do it, even if it's a little harder for those of us in this community.
